translations.answer: LATENT's state-dependent latent bound can reduce off-manifold high-level exploration while wrist correction improves racket precision, but it is a learned distribution constraint rather than a certified hardware or human-interaction safety barrier.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: A motion tracker and conditional prior cover the intended tennis states.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Human-robot racket interaction uses an independent physical safety protocol.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: LATENT tracker, high-level policy, and wrist correction.
translations.applicability.simulators.0: MJX-based training reported by the project.
translations.confidence_rationale: Large simulation evaluation and a small hardware ablation support the design; central online DAgger and high-level LAB code is not currently public, and hardware sample size is limited.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines LAB and wrist correction and reports simulation and hardware ablations.
translations.evidence.0.title: Learning Athletic Humanoid Tennis Skills from Imperfect Human Motion Data
translations.terms.2: Simulation-to-real transfer (仿真到现实迁移, sim-to-real)
translations.title: Can a Latent Action Barrier serve as the hardware safety barrier for humanoid tennis?
